elements.quote: We included randomized controlled trials (RCT) and cluster RCTs designed to evaluate the efficacy of opioids prescribed for relief of acute pain in ED- discharged patients compared to nonopioid analgesics.
elements.reason: Study designs and settings are specified, but follow-up requirements are not explicitly stated.

elements.quote: There were no exclusions based on language or date of publication. We excluded studies exclusively on patients with substance use disorder or chronic pain, evaluating only opioids given during the ED stay, comparing different opioids head- to- head, not reporting pain intensities or pain relief (after contacting authors), or available only as abstracts.
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria for language, dissemination year, and publication status (exclusion of abstracts) are explicitly specified.
The review does not distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.quote: The difference in pain intensity scores (or in pain relief) between patients who were administered opioids versus those not administered opioids from baseline to cutoff time as specified in the original RCT (the final single time point from each follow- up were used for the main analysis), adverse events incidence, utilization of rescue analgesics, and data related to patient demographics were reported for each study. If data were available for at least three studies, results for the main outcome and for adverse events were pooled and meta- analyzed. Sensitivity analyses were performed for studies with available short- term follow- up (≤3 days) to examine whether opioids were more effective in this situation. Another sensitivity analysis compared patients treated with codeine versus those treated with other opioids since codeine is a prodrug and its analgesic properties depend on its conversion to morphine, which varies considerably between subjects. Sensitivity analyses were also performed excluding studies with high risk of bias and for studies involving a pediatric population compared to adults.
elements.reason: Groups for synthesis (opioid vs non-opioid) and subgroups for sensitivity analyses are specified and linked to the review's comparisons.
No rationales are provided for the notable restrictions on study eligibility listed in the criteria.

We also searched ClinicalTrials.gov and the International Standard Randomized Controlled Trial Number registry for ongoing studies. Gray literature was searched using Google Scholar and the first 300 hits were screened to identify any relevant studies.
